relevance_note: Case report of a GFAP in-frame deletion carrier with Alexander disease plus literature tables of AxD cases: 'Based on these findings, we diagnosed the patient with Type II AxD.'
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script (scratch dir) assembled the JSON and transcribed Table 1 cells by column position, with every transcribed value checked against the table by eye and by assertion (column 7 '*' = current case, its codon p.E138_L148del, AAE 42, BS/BG/SC '+' and Bulba '-' all match the text). Table 1 (in-frame InDel cases) and Table 2 (1B-rod-domain cases) are rotated tables that the conversion garbled: in Table 1 every data row has 17 cells and aligns with the codon-change row, but the 'No.' row merges '1 2', and four codon changes (p.E207del, p.E207_K260del†, p.E243dup, p.E332del) sit in the 'Domain' row; labels use the No. values ('Table 1 #k'). Patients are columns; row labels are SC, BS, BG, SPWM, Psych, Scoli, Sleep, Urina, Motor, Bulba, AAE (Yr), AAO (Yr). The legend sits scrambled in the last column and cannot be quoted contiguously; it does not define '-' as absent, so every '-' and 'ND' is not reported and only '+' cells were recorded (observed, feature text = the row abbreviation). Checklist mapping from Table 1 only for BG (basal ganglia, defined in text as '(BG)'), SPWM (white matter), Scoli and Urina (urinary symptoms -> bladder dysfunction); SC, BS, Motor, Bulba, Sleep and Psych are composite or unspecific and were not mapped. '‡' (col 10), '§' (13,14) and '‖' (15,17) footnotes are not recoverable. Table 2 is far more garbled (merged cells such as '23 38', '* 30', '+ ND', misaligned No. row), so under the D-31 principle no phenotype, age or reference value was read from it by position. Only the 18 Table 2 people who are not also in Table 1 were added ('Table 2 #k'), with the variant from the codon row (p.E206K is displaced into the Exon row) and numbering by the order of the codon row; their source references were left not reported because the Ref row is shifted. Table 2 #3-7, #12(current case), #13 and #19 were identified with Table 1 #2-6, #7, #8 and #9 by identical variant, ages and reference cells and given no second row. Text-described literature cases were identified with Table 1 columns: 32-year-old male p.R124_L125insQLR [29] = Table 1 #2; 9-year-old male p.R126_L127insRL [30] = Table 1 #4 (AAO 9; the only RL column with 9); 71-year-old female p.R201del [31] = Table 1 #8. Contradictions/uncertainties: (1) Table reference numbers are one lower than the text's citations for the same cases (QLR: table 28 vs text [29]; RL: 29 vs [30]; R201del: 30 vs [31]), and table refs run to 47 while the converted reference list stops at 31, so both are given in source_reference_in_review for these three and the table cell alone for others. (2) Abstract says 'contrast-enhanced T2 hypointensity in the basal ganglia' and 'atrophy of ... the entire spinal cord', whereas Results say T2-hyperintensity of BG and atrophy of the cervical and thoracic SC (Fig 1j: upper cervical to middle thoracic); Results wording used. (3) Age at onset for the patient: Table 1 AAO '<20' used; text says symptoms likely since early childhood (recorded as 'odd gait' onset). (4) cDNA printed with a line-break hyphen ('...AGGGA-CAATC...' and '...GGACCT-GG') and markdown escapes; values give the 33-nt string without the hyphen and backslashes, spans keep the printed text. (5) Two intronic SNVs with rsIDs (c.1258-86 C>T, c.1171+459 A>G) are recorded as GFAP variants because the sentence places them 'in the intronic regions' after 'exon 1 of GFAP'; the authors do not discuss their significance. 'Nerve conduction study and electromyography were unremarkable' is recorded as written (excluded abnormal NCS/EMG), excluding nothing more specific (D-27). Bulbar exclusions: exam statement plus 'no bulbar symptoms or signs throughout his life'. Variant type for Table 1 cases from 'in-frame InDel mutations' (Table 1 group), left not reported for the intronic ones (Int.3/Int.4: #9, #10, #12). Father not tested; no variant row; inheritance not reported.

functional_evidence_statement.value: Mutant not reduced in stability in HEK293T cells but more in insoluble fraction; in vitro the mutant failed to form extended filaments and formed aggregates, also when mixed 1:1 with WT; aggregates in SW13 (Vim-) cells and rat primary astrocytes, with WT failing to rescue network formation (dominant effect); judged aggregation prone
span: we did not observe any noticeable decrease in expression levels of GFAP p.E138\_L148del compared to WT GFAP, indicating that this deletion mutation does not reduce GFAP protein stability
the deletion mutant failed to form extended filaments. Instead, it formed short filament-like structures that had a strong tendency to laterally associate into aggregates
Presence of WT GFAP failed to rescue the defect in GFAP network formation, suggesting a dominant effect of the deletion mutation.
the deletion mutant formed large aggregates in almost all transduced cells
All the assays revealed that GFAP p.Glu138\_Leu148del is aggregation prone.

pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors.span: We conclude that GFAP p.E138\_L148del is a pathogenic mutation responsible for the development of AxD
